I’d harden these parts next:

- [test/orders.js:18-20](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L18) `averageItemPrice` should guard against `items.length === 0`. Right now it returns `NaN` on an empty array because it divides by zero. A zero-length order is either invalid or should return a defined value.

- [test/orders.js:11-15](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L11) `applyDiscount` should validate the discount code more explicitly. As written, unknown codes are silently ignored. That may be fine, but in a backend it often hides typos or bad input. At minimum, I’d decide whether invalid codes should be rejected, logged, or treated as no-op.

- [test/orders.js:3-8](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L3) `calcTotal` should validate each item before multiplying. If an item is missing `price` or `qty`, or either is not numeric, the result becomes `NaN` and contaminates downstream output.

- [test/orders.js:23-26](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L23) `formatOrder` should handle missing or empty `order.items` and missing `order.discountCode`. Right now it assumes `order` is well-formed and that `calcTotal` succeeds, so a bad payload will throw.

- [test/orders.js:24](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L24) The string formatting should normalize money values consistently. It currently prints item prices raw, but totals with `toFixed(2)`. If prices are currency, the line items should probably use the same formatting.

- [test/orders.js:1-29](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L1) There are no exported tests or guards around edge cases. I’d add coverage for empty items, malformed items, unknown discount codes, and fractional prices so these assumptions stay stable.

If you want, I can turn that into a minimal patch set once write access is available.
